page: UpCloud PREMIUM-24xCPU-96GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The configuration provides 24 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with a shared CPU allocation model. Memory capacity totals 96.0 GB, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 400 GB local SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong compute capabilities, particularly in single-core tasks. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression tests rank in the top tier (top 10%). Multi-core stress-ng performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression are also strong, placing in the top 25%. However, memory performance presents a bottleneck; while read-only memory bandwidth is average, the large-block write bandwidth and the PassMark memory score fall into the bottom 25%. Other operations, including Redis SET transactions, static web serving, and small-to-medium LLM inference, perform within the average range.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio suitable for multi-threaded workloads that require substantial CPU capacity but do not demand extreme memory write speeds. The shared CPU allocation suggests a cost-efficient profile for high-core workloads, though it introduces potential resource contention compared to dedicated instances. This configuration is well-suited for parallel processing tasks, web serving, software compilation, and general-purpose application hosting where single-core burst performance is highly valued.
